summary: Kanti Chandra Pandey (1903–1971) worked in Indology and philosophy. He founded the University of Lucknow, where he also held a post attested in 1950.

Kapila Vatsyayan (1928–2020) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Delhi, Michigan, and Banaras Hindu University. She taught at Delhi and BHU, co-founded the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, and chaired the India International Centre.

Karam Tej Singh Sarao is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin and K. R. Norman, and became a professor at the University of Delhi in 1995.

Karel Werner (1925–2019) worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, earning a doctorate at Palacký University Olomouc. He lectured at Durham University (1969–1990) and served as a professor at Masaryk University (1993–1998).

Karen Christina Lang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who completed graduate studies at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg. She served as a professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1991–2026).
Karen Katsumoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She held posts as a part-time lecturer at Hanazono University (attested 2006) and as a lecturer at Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).

Karen McCarthy Brown (1942–2015) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Smith College, Union Theological Seminary, and Temple University. She served as a professor of anthropology at Drew University from circa 1976 to 2009.

Karen Nelson Villanueva is a scholar in religious studies and related fields. She earned a PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies and studied under traditional teachers Geshe Ngawang Dakpa and Lobsang Chökyi.
Karen Nero is an academic who held posts at the University of Canterbury around 2004 and at the University of Otago.

Karen O'Brien-Kop is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who earned her PhD at SOAS University of London. She held lectureships at the University of Roehampton (attested 2020) and King's College London (attested 2026).

Karin Meyers specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, having studied under Jay L. Garfield. She served as an assistant professor and MA program director at Kathmandu University's Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Karin Preisendanz is an Indologist and philosopher who completed her Dr. phil. and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She held positions at the University of British Columbia (1990–1993) and became a professor at the University of Vienna in 1999.

Karl Albert Agathon Benary (1807–1860) was a linguist who studied under Franz Bopp and earned a doctorate from Halle-Wittenberg. He served as a professor at Köllnisches Gymnasium (1833–1860) and as a Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin (1839).

Karl Ammer (1911–1970) worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at the University of Vienna from circa 1930 to 1935. From circa 1955 to 1970, he served as Director of the Institute of Indology at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg.

Karl Benedikt Hase (1780–1864) was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied at Jena and Helmstedt. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (1816–1864), and the Faculty of Arts of Paris.

Karl Brugmann (1849–1919) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Georg Curtius at the University of Leipzig. He served as a professor at the University of Freiburg (1884) and the University of Leipzig (1887–1919).

Karl Brunnhölzl is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under several traditional teachers, including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Khenpo Lama Thubten.

Karl Debreczeny is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Hung Wu and Jenny Purtle, and served as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2008).

Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal (1812–1894) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Heidelberg, and later held a post at Heidelberg University from circa 1836 to 1842.

Karl Eugen Neumann (1865–1915) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Leipzig from circa 1887 to 1888 and completed his doctoral studies under Richard Pischel from circa 1888 to 1891.
